red.local: Two component tests failed before service-CA TLS and current-generation readiness were implemented.
live: MLflow rejected the initial plaintext PostgreSQL service because SSL was required.
MLflow rejected the first TLS endpoint because its trusted bundle did not contain the OpenShift service CA.

security.network_policy: only pods labeled app=mlflow may reach TCP 5432
security.credential_rotation: completed after diagnostic exposure; replacement value was neither printed nor committed

proof_model.TDD: The service-CA and observed-generation contracts were captured RED before implementation and pass GREEN.
proof_model.EDD: This manifest records the commit, cluster, versions, digests, database state, TLS session, and operator conditions.
proof_model.CDD: The MLflow CR consumes both its backend URI and CA bundle through named Kubernetes objects.
proof_model.BDD: Given the shared MLflow service uses the PostgreSQL Secret, MLflow starts only after verified TLS succeeds and serves healthy requests.
proof_model.CBT: PostgreSQL TLS, CA injection, persistence, network isolation, disruption budget, MLflow readiness, and schema creation were checked independently.

limitations: MLflow artifacts remain on a single ReadWriteOnce file-backed PVC; an external object store is required before HA replicas.
This shared-service proof does not promote AgentOps beyond its one-seat cap.
Pipeline database TLS, production Logging storage, five-seat load, twenty-five-seat load, public access, and external trusted TLS remain separate gates.
